text:
alex: Heads up — canary-12 shows a host-side CPU jump ~18% and p95 +25ms after the "microcodec packing" change. Not obvious in GPU traces, looks like pre-infer overhead. Anyone digging? :eyes:
infra-bot: alert: canary-12 ingress_cpu_spike > threshold (link: https://ops.redwood/canary/12)
priya: saw the alert, grabbed a pprof from the host side. early look: tokenize + proto unpack hot. dropping flame sample:
```
pprof flame (host):
 - host::tokenize 42%
 - parse::proto_unpack 28%
 - staging::coalesce 6%
 - socket::read 4%
```
alex: interesting — tokenize dominates. microcodec packs more small records into frames; perhaps extra copy / re-parse overhead?
jon_s: my hunch: kernel selection heuristics use seq_len_hist and batch shape sampling. microcodec altered observed seq distribution (more short fragments), so runtime picks a different kernel path (not necessarily faster). can we check kernel chooser logs?
samira: also seeing KV cache hitrate dip on canary-12: was ~87% baseline -> ~72% now. suspect microcodec makes more unique prefix keys (frame boundaries differ) -> more misses / warmup.
priya: grabbing kernel chooser trace and kv metrics. kernel-chooser.log shows a switch at 11:42:12 where batcher favored kernel_id=7 for short sequences.
jon_s: kernel_id=7 is the "packed_vector" kernel that is great for contiguous token blocks but awful when input is many short segments (context churn). if microcodec increases segment count, that explains regression. quick experiment: force kernel_id=3 for seq<128 and re-run canary.
alex: good call. two short-term options: revert microcodec packing, or change ingress preparse to coalesce small frames before handing off to tokenizer. prefer non-revert if small coalesce fixes it.
priya: I'll prototype a 8ms coalesce window (was 2ms) in ingress preparse to join tiny frames. patch queued: canary-13.
deploy-bot: deploy planned: priya/ingress-coalesce -> canary-13 (link: https://ci.redwood/build/2345)
samira: I'm running KV trace now. early log snippet showing miss spike:
```
[2024-07-03T11:41:55Z] kv_client GET miss key=ctx:rq:abcd123 size=64
[2024-07-03T11:41:56Z] kv_client GET miss key=ctx:rq:efgh456 size=48
[2024-07-03T11:41:56Z] kv_client EVICT key=ctx:rq:oldkey
```
samira: eviction rate up ~3x in the few minutes after canary deploy. that would raise host CPU as we rehydrate KV and re-warm caches.
jon_s: also tweak batching heuristic: if we detect many short segments per connection, prefer larger micro-batches (higher batching window) to amortize tokenize costs. we can flip a config flag for canary.
alex: action list: 1) priya: ingress coalesce patch -> canary-13 (8ms window) 2) jon_s: kernel override experiment (force kernel_id=3 for seq<128) 3) samira: complete KV trace and share heatmap 4) infra: monitor canary-13 CPU, KV hitrate, p95.
priya: rolling canary-13 now. will post results in 15m. :thumbsup:
jon_s: I'll queue kernel override on a small subset (tag canary-13-kernel-test).
samira: if coalesce + kernel override don't recover, we should consider fallback: microcodec optional flag off for canary-12 tenants. but hope not.
alex: agreed. try non-invasive fixes first. keep updates short here. tagging @eng-sre if we need node pool scaling.
deploy-bot: canary-13 deployed to 10 hosts at 1759504470 by priya.
priya: initial numbers from canary-13 (5m window): host CPU drop ~9% vs canary-12, p95 down by ~12ms, KV hitrate up to 83%. still not baseline but improving. more metrics forthcoming.
samira: KV heatmap shows evictions reduced; coalesce seems to reduce unique prefix churn.
jon_s: kernel override recovered another ~6ms p95 in quick run. looks like both changes are additive.
alex: great — let's keep canary-13 running and collect 1h of telemetry. if stable, we can promote and land an ingress coalesce and kernel-chooser fallback. thanks all.
priya: will post final graph and followup PR.
infra-bot: note: alert cleared for canary-13.
alex: closing loop later with postmortem if this shows up in prod. for now: monitoring.
